newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close flat, smaller firms in demand.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close flat, smaller firms in demand.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed on Friday a shade lower on consolidation after the recent bull-run, but rotational buying boosted smaller-capitalised companies, brokers said.
Kia Group shares recovered from the initial shock of financial trouble rumours in the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate, they said.
"Many blue chips remained weak but sporadic buying interest focused on smaller-cap shares," said Kim Myung-ho at Hyundai Securities. "The market will consolidate another two weeks."
The composite stock index lost 0.73 of a point to 770.22. The small-cap sub-index gained 26.58 points to 1,963.76.
Brokers said the slow pace of the yen's rise against the dollar and slightly rising interest rates have accelerated consolidation in large-capitalised shares.
Samsung Electronics lost 1,000 won to 70,000 and POSCO shed 1,300 won to 60,500.
Lee Hee-myong at Samsung Securities said: "The consolidation seemed to be almost at the end. Rotational buying is expected to boost large-cap shares again next week."
"Smaller-cap shares will face profit-taking tomorrow. It's the right time to buy blue chips at low price," said Park Key-pyong at Hanyang Securities.
Recent laggards among smaller-cap shares were spotlighted. Pyung Hwa Industry went limit up to 51,600 won. Shindo Ricoh gained 4,000 won to 55,300.

Info-tech companies were highlighted in the belief those companies had good growth potential. LG Information and Communication gained 2,500 won to 107,500 and Hansol Telecom added 3,000 won to 41,000.
The fall in Kia Group shares was halted but brokers said the shares would remain weak for the time being.
Asia Motors gained 240 won to 4,270 and Kia Motors rose 500 won to 13,600.
"Many investors believe Kia affiliates will hardly default and have escaped from the early jitters," Kim of Hyundai said.
But Lee of Samsung said a sell-off by foreign investors and sluggish domestic car sales would force local investors to shy away from Kia shares.
The Securities Supervisory Board said foreign investors became net sellers of stocks on Friday as they sold 56 billion won worth of Korean stocks and bought 47.5 billion.
Dong Ah Construction shed 200 won to 17,700 on the news that the construction ministry had revoked the company's licence to build steel-framed bridges.
